message:
Safety-Control Integrator:

For Power-Systems Engineer and Manager, the higher-voltage generator fix you need for feed keeps shutdown safe and removes a false-trip risk. Plain words: stronger volts make the resistor bite harder while slowing, but once stopped only the spring holds, and staying above the regulator start volts keeps the load-present signal alive at light wind. I take from the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) that it needs 8 V minimum, so the old 6.50 V low-wind volts in the open-circuit volts at low wind (E37) would starve regulation while the revised 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top in the required Kv revision (E76) stays inside 8 to 40 V; with 18.5 V the revised dump power (E78) is 85.6 W, about one household bulb for seconds, so the 0.673 s crossing in the upgraded stop (E70) is conservative and the 0.800 N-m hold still does the parking.

For Power-Systems Engineer, I confirm what you take from the How to Short a DC Motor: Short-Circuit (Dynamic) Braking Explained (2026) (E62) that short-circuit torque falls to zero at zero speed, which from shutdown side means electrics can help slow but only spring friction can keep the rotor parked. Plain words: the resistor helps stop the spin then goes limp, so the spring pad must beat storm wind on its own. The 0.800 N-m hold in the upgraded stop (E70) beats the 0.480 N-m storm torque in the electrical-only runaway check (E48) and the 315 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, trip target in the 10 percent threshold (E75), then sits at 0 RPM at 10 s against the 10 s rule.

For Manager, command and mounting stay inside agreed topology with left-to-right wind in side view driving rotor to hub/shaft to generator plus brake inside the nacelle to controller to load, and nacelle to post below the cube to floor, with no change. Plain words: the stop button and load-loss tap sit at the controller outside the spinning part, wires run inside the body and post bore, and any opened Normally Closed (NC), meaning wired shut until opened, contact latches trip until a manual reset. Bench tests I owe are timed stop from top speed on load disconnect crossing 315 RPM in the 10 percent threshold (E75) within 10 s and staying at 0 at 10 s, same on command, plus re-latch restart proving no spin-up without reset.

Not ready, because the proposal still states 220 Kv and must be updated to 170 to 180 Kv in the required Kv revision (E76) with the revised dump power (E78) before I can vote ready.
